subject: MAP update — legal redlines ownership and handback timelines
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + legal redlines ownership (post-demo follow-up)

Evan — thanks again for the demo and the time today. Attached is the MAP v0.2 I promised (Nimbus-MAP-v0.2.xlsx). This version pulls together the milestones we discussed and the suggested owners. Key ask here is to align on the Legal redlines milestone so both sides know who will own edits, turnaround times, and blockers.

Highlights from the call: 
- Target close: 2027-04-08 (customer indicated end-of-Q2 preference; we proposed 4/8 to leave margin)
- MAP milestone we want to lock this week: "Legal redlines: MSA/DPA/SLA negotiation"
- Proposed ownership and TAT (suggested):
  - Redwood initial redline pass (owner: Redwood Legal / Ben Carter): 48 business hours after receiving customer's redlines
  - Customer redline receipt and counter: 72 business hours
  - Repeat cycles: target max 3 cycles before exec escalation

Dependencies called out: procurement PO, SOC2 attestation docs (customer requested), and any product-architecture clarifications on data residency (if they push on private deployment).

Please confirm: who will be Nimbus Health's legal lead for redlines and whether 72h is reasonable. Also confirm whether they prefer our standard MSA template (attached) as a starting point — that typically reduces cycles.

Attachments: Nimbus-MAP-v0.2.xlsx, MSA_standard_template.docx

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + legal redlines ownership (post-demo follow-up)

Diego — thanks for the recap and the MAP. Appreciate the clear owners/TATs. A few quick notes from legal/procurement side: 

- I'll loop in our legal ops lead, Samantha Li (cc'ed). She will be the point for receiving the initial redline and coordinating internal review.
- 72 business hours for the first counter is reasonable for us as long as we have the MSA template and a short change-log (helps speed up review).
- Dependencies: procurement will need a short SOW and an indicative license/headcount itemization to approve the PO — I can get procurement in parallel but it will add ~3 business days once they see the SOW.

We should also surface the SLA targets explicitly in the MAP (p99, degraded failover) — Samantha, can you confirm if we need any additional security artifacts beyond SOC2 (e.g., pen test report)?

I'll ask Samantha to aim for a 72h turnaround on our first counter after we receive Redwood's initial redline. If we hit any unusual clauses (data residency, deletion certs), that might add time.

— Evan
Head of Partnerships, Nimbus Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimhealth.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + legal redlines ownership (post-demo follow-up)

Looping in Redwood Legal's approach. Agree with Diego's proposed TATs; to minimize cycles, we'll use our standard MSA template as suggested — attached is a redline-tracker stub (MSA_redlines_tracker.xlsx) that we'll keep live.

Commitments from our side: 
- Redwood initial pass: Ben Carter (Legal) — 48 business hours from receipt of Nimbus redlines (if we receive by EOD, will aim to return within 2 business days)
- We’ll flag any non-standard clauses (data residency, indemnity caps, source-code escrow requests) on first pass and propose language or escalation points.
- If the customer provides a heavy redline (full counter-MSA), we'll provide an estimate of cycles and propose a short call within 24h of the first counter to walk the key items — this often speeds things up.

Attachments: MSA_redlines_tracker.xlsx

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimhealth.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft + legal redlines ownership (post-demo follow-up) — confirmed owners & next steps

Thanks everyone — quick recap and firmed-up MAP milestone entries so we have a single source of truth: 

MAP milestone: Legal redlines — MSA/DPA/SLA negotiation- Owner (Redwood): Ben Carter (Legal) — initial pass TAT: 48 business hours- Owner (Nimbus Health): Samantha Li (Legal Ops) — counter TAT: 72 business hours- Dependencies: Procurement SOW (Nimbus), SOC2 report (Redwood / available), final list of required SLAs (p50/p95/p99), data residency requirement- Escalation: after 3 full redline cycles, Diego (sales) + Ben (legal) will request an exec touchpoint with Nimbus (Evan) to unblock- Target close for deal: 2027-04-08

Action items (owner / due):
- Nimbus: confirm procurement SOW timeline; provide any special data residency language by 2027-03-07 (Samantha)
- Redwood: send initial redline pass once we have Nimbus's first counter; meanwhile attach our standard MSA as baseline (Ben) — Redwood will prepare the first-pass template if Nimbus prefers us to start
- Product/Eng on standby: Marissa to answer technical SLA/data questions within 24h when asked (Marissa)

Next sync: short 30-min redlines sync on 2027-03-08 at 10:00 AM PT (proposed) — confirm if that works for Nimbus.

Attachments referenced: Nimbus-MAP-v0.2.xlsx, MSA_redlines_tracker.xlsx, MSA_standard_template.docx

Diego Fernandez
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
